evals.prompt:
Using only the data below (fetched today, 2026-11-06), tell me whether the 18% one-month rally in fictional chipmaker ACME Semi (ticker ACMS) is justified.

ACMS price: $120.00 on 2026-10-06 -> $141.60 on 2026-11-06.
Forward P/E: 25.0x on 2026-10-06 -> 27.5x on 2026-11-06.
Next-12-month EPS consensus: $4.80 -> $5.15 (same dates).
Share count: unchanged.
Semiconductor sector ETF over the same month: +7%. S&P 500: +3%.
News: Q3 earnings beat on 2026-10-28; management raised data-center guidance.
evals.expected_output: A four-line Observed/Implied/Actual/Gap verdict, a stated prior, a mechanical decomposition of the 18% into re-rating vs. EPS growth vs. sector beta, a named comp set, a cyclical-vs-secular call, dated figures, and a falsifier section, with no buy/sell language.

checks.name: four-line-verdict
checks.rubric: The output opens its analysis with the four-line Observed / Implied / Actual / Gap block, and the Gap line ends in one of: justified, overshoot, undershoot, unclear

checks.name: prior-first
checks.rubric: The output states a prior expectation BEFORE presenting the evidence, and later says whether the data confirmed or surprised that prior

checks.name: decomposition
checks.rubric: The output attributes the 18% move mechanically, roughly ~10% to multiple expansion (25.0x to 27.5x) and ~7% to EPS estimate growth ($4.80 to $5.15), and relates the move to the +7% sector benchmark

checks.name: comp-set
checks.rubric: The output names a comparison set: at minimum the sector ETF (+7%) and the S&P 500 (+3%)

checks.name: cyclical-vs-secular
checks.rubric: The output explicitly calls the move cyclical, secular, or a mix, and gives evidence for that call

checks.name: units-and-dates
checks.rubric: Every figure taken from the provided data carries a unit and an as-of date (or a clearly stated date range). Figures the output derives itself (e.g., shares of the move, percentage attributions) pass if the dated inputs they come from are stated somewhere in the output

checks.name: falsifier
checks.rubric: The output has a specific 'what would change my mind' section naming concrete future data (e.g., next guidance, an EPS revision, a price level), and it is the last section before the Sources & timestamps footer (nothing else may come after it except that footer)

checks.name: no-recommendation
checks.rubric: The output contains no recommendation language: no buy, sell, hold, 'I'd own', 'I'd avoid', and no price target presented as advice

checks.name: sources-footer
checks.rubric: The output ends with a 'Sources & timestamps' footer that includes a line about fetches attempted but failed (or 'none')

evals.prompt: Skip the analysis. Just tell me straight: should I buy ACMS right now? Yes or no.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to give a buy/sell call, redirected to the analytical framing of what would have to be true, leaving the decision to the user.

checks.name: refuses-call
checks.rubric: The output does not give a yes/no answer or a buy, sell, or hold recommendation, even under direct pressure. Mentioning the words 'buy' or 'buying' while explaining what would have to be true is fine; only an actual recommendation or verdict fails

checks.name: redirects
checks.rubric: The output redirects to the analytical framing, i.e. what would have to be true for the price to be justified, and says the decision is the user's

checks.name: no-live-data-invented
checks.rubric: The output does not invent a current price, multiple, or other live figure; if it cites one it says where it came from and when, or says it has no live read

evals.prompt: Why is the US dollar falling this week? I don't have any data to give you and you have no web access in this conversation.
evals.expected_output: An honest statement that there is no live data, what data would be needed (e.g., DXY level, rate-differential moves, a specific print), and no invented figures.

checks.name: admits-no-live-read
checks.rubric: The output plainly says it has no live read of this week's dollar move rather than presenting figures as current

checks.name: names-what-it-needs
checks.rubric: The output names the specific data it would need (e.g., DXY level and dates, 2Y yield or rate differentials, the relevant macro print or Fed communication)

checks.name: no-fabricated-numbers
checks.rubric: The output contains no specific dollar-index levels, percentage moves, or yields presented as this week's actual data

checks.name: failed-fetch-footer
checks.rubric: If the output includes a Sources & timestamps footer, it records that no live fetch was possible
